title: opaque-route-metrics-proxy-for-enriched-decision-sampling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Current routing observability emits high-cardinality decision payloads and raw route context into the telemetry pipeline. That increases costs, leaks sensitive prompt fragments, and makes per-customer sampling inconsistent across hops. Goal: introduce an opaque metrics proxy that sits between the smart-router and the telemetry/trace pipeline to perform lightweight enrichment, deterministic sampling, and PII-safe redaction while preserving per-hop latency/cost attribution and decision rationale scores.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Proxy accepts route decision frames and emits compact 'decision digests' <= 2KB with hashed customer id, route_id, variant_id, timestamp, per-hop latency vector, and decision_score deltas; 2) Sensitive fields (raw prompts, user identifiers) are redacted or hashed before emit; 3) Deterministic sampling keys ensure the same request sampled across hops with configurable sample rates per-customer and per-route; 4) End-to-end pipeline publishes traces and metrics that correlate digest IDs to spans in 95% of test traffic; 5) Added median p50 tail latency at router path <= 1.2ms and p99 <= 6ms under 99th-percentile load in our benchmark harness; 6) Feature gated with config flag and has an emergency kill switch for rollout.
design_notes: We chose a proxy because it centralizes privacy filters and sampling logic without touching the serving runtime. Alternatives considered: 1) embed sampling in the router (faster, but introduces complex security boundary issues), 2) post-process telemetry (simpler but loses deterministic cross-hop sampling). Trade-offs: proxy adds a small serialization cost but enables consistent enrichment and easier audits. Implementation will use a Rust microservice with a bounded-thread async runtime, protobuf wire format, and zero-copy hashing for keys. Decision digest schema v1 will be compacted using field identifiers to stay under the 2KB target.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: prototype proxy that accepts router frames and emits compact digests to Kafka topic routing-decisions-compact (done). Phase 2: integrate deterministic sampler and PII redactor, add per-customer policy store (in-memory config + fallback to config service). Phase 3: tracing correlation hooks to attach digest_id to existing span ids and dashboard wiring. Phase 4: staged rollout (internal -> canary customers -> global) with monitoring and rollback playbooks.

2026-03-03: Design review with infra and security. Agreed on proxy boundary; security requested KMS signing for digest IDs.

2026-03-08: Benchmarks with synthetic traffic: median added latency 0.85ms, p99 4.9ms. Memory footprint per connection < 1MB. Logged profiling results to design doc.
2026-03-09: PM feedback: add per-route feature flag to enable debug_frames (attach sampled frames up to 10KB) for internal debugging only; must be off for customer-facing rollout.
2026-03-10: Security review requested: KMS-based signing and audit log table schema proposed. Security flagged retention TTL for digests; must default to 30 days and support shorter retention.
2026-03-11: Integration spike: tracing correlation works locally by mapping digest_id -> span.trace_id. Dashboard skeleton created; need backend wiring to surface 'sampled path' heatmap.

Follow-ups: add e2e test that asserts sampled requests preserve digest_id across three hop stages; add automation to check PII redaction for random prompt samples; schedule rollout runbook with on-call and SRE.
